source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #287 (branch fix/285-barrier-tail-dispatch at head c308c156e0a1f48683590433f1075c97f9bf8a3e — branch commit fb0ea07 (restore tail dispatch at every #240 identity-barrier handler except op_return (#285)) plus merge commit c308c15 bringing in current main 3be9627, so the pull-request run built the same tree; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45196676309 and 45196700235 against the branch and pull-request run 45194029095, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #287 (#285, all 264 identity-barrier handlers dispatch non-tail: the #240 identity barrier at the 41 remaining source sites — 38 in memory.rs (33 macro-generated plus 5 direct), 2 in simd.rs (the f32x4/f64x2 replace-lane handlers) and 1 in numeric.rs (op_i32_crc16_update16_masked) — is replaced with the volatile-load form proven in #277/#282, restoring tail dispatch for the whole handler set; op_return keeps its black_box as the one intentional exception because its dispatch target is terminal and no frame accumulates; op_f64_const and op_ref_is_null are untouched here, being the scope of PRs #283 and #286). The branch merged current main (3be9627, containing PR #283) before measurement; the merge was conflict-free, and op_f64_const's volatile load from PR #283 is present exactly once afterwards, verified in source and by a full disassembly audit of the merged tree (CLI: 261 TAIL / 1 NONTAIL, the only NONTAIL being op_return). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (3be9627) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45196725415, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 32 gated series, so every delta is this PR's own. 28 of the 32 gated series change; only the baseline configuration is byte-identical in both profiles. In release, stripped .text grows by +1,728 B in core, component, core-aot, core-nosimd and wasi and by +2,112 B in wasi-threads, while core-jit shrinks by −2,368 B; stripped file grows by +3,984 B (core, component, core-aot, wasi), +3,968 B (core-nosimd), +4,896 B (wasi-threads) and +128 B (core-jit). In release-size, stripped .text grows by +1,248 B (wasi), +1,264 B (core, component, core-aot, wasi-threads), +1,280 B (core-nosimd) and +2,000 B (core-jit), and stripped file grows by +8,064 B (core, component, core-aot, wasi), +8,080 B (core-nosimd, wasi-threads) and +9,856 B (core-jit). Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth remains the release-size component stripped .text series at +5.47% (1,169,031 B to 1,232,999 B), up from +5.36%. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series across the three samples.
